transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic? What's been going on that made you decide to come see me?

I'm here because... well, I just can't seem to keep my work straight lately. I work at a dry cleaner's, and it's just getting to be too much. The tickets, the receipts, the notes from the workshop... it all just piles up. I look at it and I just... I don't even know what to handle first anymore. It's just a mess.
Over the past few weeks, have you been feeling persistently sad, down, or hopeless? Or have you been experiencing a lot of worry or anxiety?
No, I wouldn't say that. I'm not sad or anything. Just... having trouble keeping up at work. I don't really worry more than anyone else, I guess.
Have you always had trouble organizing things and keeping track of details, even back in school or in other jobs before this one?

I suppose so, yeah. Um... even back in grade school. My teachers used to tell my mom that I was... well, bright, but scattered. I was always losing my papers and... they'd have to remind me to finish my work. And they said I talked out of turn a lot, too. So... yeah, I guess it's always been like this.

When you're trying to work on those tasks at the dry cleaner's, do you find yourself fidgeting, restless, or having trouble sitting still? Or do you tend to rush through things and make careless mistakes?

I'm not really sure. I mean, I'm on my feet most of the day at the counter anyway, so... I don't really notice if I'm restless. And... I guess mistakes happen sometimes, but I don't know if I'm rushing. Just... I don't know. normal mistakes, I think.

Besides the trouble organizing things at work, have you been experiencing any physical symptoms or health concerns that have been bothering you — like pain, fatigue, or other bodily sensations that worry you?
No, not really. Physically, I feel fine. Just... normal, I guess. Nothing like that.
When you're working on something that requires focus — like sorting through those tickets and receipts — do you find it hard to keep your attention on it, or do you get distracted easily?

Yeah... I guess I do. I mean, I'll start going over the day's orders just fine, but... after a few minutes, my mind just kind of wanders off. I'll start thinking about, I don't know, the clothing labels, or choir plans, or just stuff at home. And then... I look down and realize I missed half of what I was supposed to check.
When you're doing tasks that require sitting down and concentrating, like reviewing those receipts, do you feel a need to get up and move around, or do you find it hard to stay in one place?

I guess... yeah. Like, when we have church committee meetings, or... those fabric-care trainings for work. I just... I end up getting up a lot. I'll go get water, or say I need to grab some papers, or just check on something. Even when everyone else is just... sitting there. It's just hard to stay put for that long.
Going back to when you were a child — in elementary school or middle school — did you have trouble paying attention and staying focused on schoolwork even then, or did that start more recently?

I suppose so, yes. Um... even back in grade school, my teachers would tell my mother that I was... bright, but scattered. I was always talking out of turn, or... losing my papers. They were always having to remind me to just finish my work. So... yeah, it's been a long time.

When you think back to elementary school — say, around age 7 or 8 — were you already having these kinds of problems with attention and sitting still back then, or do you remember things being different?

I mean... like I just said, it was happening in grade school. I don't really remember exactly if I was seven or eight. It's... it's been a long time. I just know my teachers were always getting onto me, like I mentioned. I don't really remember much else from back then.
When you were in elementary school, before you turned 12 years old, would you say these problems with paying attention and needing to move around were already happening back then?
Yes. Like I said... elementary school is before twelve. So, yes. It was already happening. I really don't have anything else to add about it.

Besides the trouble at work with organizing and focusing, have these problems with attention and sitting still caused you significant difficulty in other areas of your life — like in your relationships, social activities, or managing things at home?

I suppose so. At the laundry shop, it's... well, we've had some late orders. And some mix-ups with the billing. It causes some tense moments with the staff, and sometimes the customers. And... at church, I used to help plan things, but I stepped back. People were just getting frustrated with me. So, yes. It affects things.
